observationsNotFindings: The branch recital writes the second span as an unbroken 'D-237 through D-308' and then removes D-272 by an adjacent express sentence, whereas the fourteen adopted entries D-295 through D-308 each break the span arithmetically ('D-237 through D-271 and D-273 through D-<prev>') while carrying the same carve-out sentence. I examined this as a candidate SHOULD-FIX and it does not survive: the carve-out sentence is unambiguous and load-bearing, the resulting membership is exactly correct, the prompt states the branch in the same unbroken-plus-carve-out form, and range-then-exception is a well-formed construction. It is a form variance against recent house practice, not a false claim, so I record it here rather than as a finding. A future entry may prefer the arithmetic break for uniformity.
The turn-2 draft's branch endpoint correctly advances to D-308 — the last adopted entry — rather than to the entry under draft, matching how D-308 itself ended at D-307.

Two files in the tree carry an 08 prefix. Selecting the wrong one produces a spurious file-08-moved OBJECT. The prompt's digest disambiguates, but a future prompt naming the path alongside the digest would remove the trap entirely.

The Claude Stage A signed-index leftover-join.v8 review inverts the advisories/blockers presence pattern of the other two Claude Stage A reviews — it omits advisories and carries an empty blockers list, where the others carry empty advisories and omit blockers. The disposition table tracks the inversion correctly rather than normalizing it, which is the behavior that makes these rows worth reciting at all.

The subject carries two distinct unlabeled Codex SHOULD-FIXes without conflating them: the Stage A one landed at signed-index leftover-join.v8 (line 69) and the Stage B turn-1 one landed in this draft's Decision (line 81). Both are named as unlabeled and neither receives an invented identifier.

OD-112-3 is described consistently as a policy rather than a number in all three places it appears, which is what keeps it out of the OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS remainder.

conclusion: Independent adversarial review of the D-309 turn-2 draft against its own bytes and the live tree. The subject digest matched c73b08c6... at open and again at verdict write, mode 0444 throughout; the subject did not move. All thirteen path-and-digest pairs the draft asserts recompute exactly, and each of the six Stage A reviews cites the digest of the artifact D-309 actually records, so every ACCEPT 0/0 attaches to the recorded bytes. The assigned turn-2 question resolves cleanly: the unlabeled Codex turn-1 SHOULD-FIX is landed in the exact speaker-qualified form Codex's narrowRemedy asked for, it appears in both the Protocol recital and the Decision, no unqualified occupancy denial survives, and the G08 occupancy v7 recording Codex asked be preserved is intact — with no identifier minted for it. Both turn-1 review recitals are exact, including Codex's ten-member shouldFix enumeration and the absence of an id member. All six Stage A disposition rows are exact across three distinct absent-field patterns. leftoverDesign remains [OBL-G08-FX-AUTHORING, OBL-RESERVED-NUMBERS], unflipped. Register tokens are preserved unflattened (DR-112 OPEN, DR-G08 OPEN, DR-118 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, DR-107 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW), required-now stays 28, and both readiness figures verify. Every named attack fails against the bytes. I developed one candidate SHOULD-FIX — the branch recital states an unbroken D-237 through D-308 span where fourteen adopted precedents break it arithmetically at D-272 — and discharged it: the adjacent carve-out sentence makes the membership unambiguous and correct, so it is a form variance, recorded as an observation. No MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX survive verification.
